evidence.text: - Resolve instructions in printed order, doing as much as possible. Inability to perform one instruction does not prohibit playing or using a Power on an otherwise legal target. evidence.text: Matching lands with Invaders Ravage. Total the Damage: **1 per Explorer +2 per Town +3 per City**, then apply Defend and other explicit modifiers. **Defend N** reduces each occurrence of Invader Damage to both land and Dahan by N for this turn, to a minimum of zero. Multiple Defend effects add. It does not reduce Spirit Damage or make Dahan do less counterattack Damage. Land and Dahan receive the reduction separately, not by splitting a shared allowance. requested_parts: Whether Explorer survives retained Damage and why.

answers.answer: The replacement itself causes no Fear. The Explorer retains the Town’s 1 marked Damage; because the Explorer has Health 1, that Damage destroys it, generating the Explorer’s 0 destruction Fear. Reduced Health can also destroy a previously damaged piece without new Damage.

evidence.text: “Damage” means **Damage to Invaders** unless explicitly stated otherwise. Normal Spirit Damage does not harm Dahan or the land. Distribute Damage among Invaders in the target land however you wish; Explorers need not be hit first. Damage from separate normal Powers and counterattacks can accumulate within a turn. A piece is destroyed immediately when its marked Damage reaches/exceeds its Health. Reduced Health can also destroy a previously damaged piece; Damage does not itself reduce Health. Marked Damage does not reduce the Health counted by a Health-worth removal allowance. If a damaged piece moves out of a Health bonus or into a Health penalty and is thereby destroyed, destruction occurs in its destination land, never in an in-between location. [FAQ if-an-invader-with-health-bonus-and-damage-is-moved-where-is-it-destroyed]

**Destroy** returns pieces to supply regardless of Health when directly instructed. Every destroyed Town generates **1 Fear** and every destroyed City **2 Fear**, in addition to explicit Fear from the effect. Explorers generate none automatically. **Remove** returns the specified pieces without requiring Damage to reach their Health and without destruction Fear. Within the effect's count and piece-type restrictions, its decision-maker may choose any eligible pieces; there is no Explorer-first priority unless stated. **Replace** removes a piece and adds another, retaining its marked Damage: the replacement itself produces no Fear, but if the retained Damage destroys the new piece, destruction Fear applies normally. For simultaneous replacements, select all pieces before replacing any: the same original City cannot become a Town and then an Explorer within that one simultaneous instruction. Separate completed instructions or actions may replace the resulting piece again (e.g., successive players resolving **Trade Suffers** at Terror III).

| Explorer | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| Town | 2 | 2 | 1 |
| City | 3 | 3 | 2 |
| Dahan | 2 | 2 in counterattack | 0 |

evidence.text: - Unless explicitly different, use **one target land or Spirit, once per turn**. Multiple effects and all innate levels apply to that same target. You cannot pay twice for an ordinary card use or use an innate twice just by having twice its Elements.

requested_parts: Difference between Move Presence and Add Presence/reposition.
Whether the source disk may be outside the shown destination Range.
answers.answer: Move Presence moves a specified disk from its current location by the shown distance. Add Presence places a track disk at a legal destination; it can also reposition an island disk, but first measures the destination’s Range from existing Presence (including that disk). Once the destination is selected within Range, the disk may be taken from anywhere on the island, so its former location need not be within the shown Range.

evidence.text: - **Move Presence:** A curved movement arrow moves the specified Presence from its present location up to the shown distance; this differs from Add/reposition. Push/Gather Presence uses normal adjacency rules. Instructions are mandatory where possible; a move up to a Range can be zero.

- **Add Presence:** Choose a legal land within the shown maximum Range of your existing Presence. Take the leftmost remaining disk from either Presence track and add it there. With multiple placements, resolve them sequentially: a newly placed disk may be the origin for the next. You may instead **reposition any of your island Presence**, even with track disks remaining: first measure range and select the destination using existing Presence, including the disk about to be repositioned, then take a disk from anywhere on the island. This is still an Add Presence instruction, not a Move instruction. Destroyed Presence cannot be used unless explicitly permitted.

clause_coverage_check.ruling: Move shifts specified Presence a shown distance; Add places/repositions as instructed.
Destination range is checked; disk may be taken from anywhere on island.

requested_parts: Whether Gift of Strength/Powerstorm Repeat card choice is immediate.
Whether Slow card can be selected.
Whether card’s printed Elements are gained again.
answers.answer: Powerstorm and Gift of Strength give a once-this-turn option, so the card may be chosen when the Repeat is exercised rather than at grant time; a later-played card may qualify while in play and within restrictions. A Slow card can be repeated but resolves using its most recently assigned speed. These permissions repeat Power Cards, not Innates. A Repeat grants no additional printed card Elements.

evidence.text: Retain changes to the Power, including extra Range or changed speed. An ordinary Repeat uses the Power's **most recently assigned speed**: a Slow Power repeats in Slow even if its permission came from a Fast Power; a formerly Fast Power explicitly made Slow before repeating now repeats in Slow. An instruction to Repeat immediately instead follows that explicit timing, directly after the originating use. [FAQ repeating-powers-with-changed-speeds] You may postpone choosing which eligible card to repeat until you actually repeat it, and make different choices/targets then. For **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength**, the Spirit receives a once-this-turn option rather than a grant-time selection of cards: a card played later that turn may be selected while it remains in play, subject to the permission’s restrictions and cost. [FAQ timing-of-choosing-powers-for-once-this-turn-repeats] Gift of Strength imposes its printed card-cost eligibility ceiling but requires no additional Energy payment for the Repeat, so an eligible card may be repeated with no Energy left. If the permission requires paying a cost, pay it as instructed. **Powerstorm** requires paying the repeated Power Card's Energy cost again when exercising each Repeat, including its threshold's further permissions; the original play payment does not cover it.

A Repeat activates a Power's effects again; it is not a second card play and grants no additional printed card Elements. It **does** count as another Power use. For effects counting cards played (such as Boon of Vigor), a Repeat adds no card play; count the card's original play only. A repeated effect explicitly granting Elements grants those again. Recheck thresholds using your current Elements; they were not spent on the original, but may since have been lost.

- **Repeat limits:** **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength** repeat Power **Cards**, not Innates. Powerstorm's threshold repeats up to three **different** cards. A Range/Speed change granted by a threshold carries to a Repeat even if that threshold is no longer met; it does not stack the same Range bonus again. [Core: .3y28aex, .7w4g8q9, Repeating-internal-range-boosts]
